searchText: Well, in this particular case the goal of this channel is to *create* the official info 😆 (since in the last ACD call we agreed to figure it out offline before the next call) Does anyone oppose the Aug 4 date? Do we need to delay to the 4th? Tim originally had this block cued up for July 28. That's three weeks from the last testnet Would be cool to have it on the mainnet in time for the sixth anniversary of Ethereum's initial release on July 30 London is a tremendous accomplishment, and I can't wait to see it on the mainnet I also *weakly* favor sooner rather than later unless there is some reason where we believe we would benefit from an extra week on testnets. Is there any particular data we are hoping to collect by running in testnet for longer? Is there something that some client hasn't finished but is likely to be able to finish with an extra week? I'm inclined towards Aug 4. London is a major accomplishment and if an extra week helps smoother implementation, I'm all for it. Given the issues with the gas limit setting I think an extra week (aug 4 date) for more messaging to operators instead of more time for client development should be strongly considered. I think it's unfortunate more hasn't been done on this front since we've known about this quirk of the upgrade since at least early may, and now it's contributing to a delay of the fork if it gets out to twitter that we're delaying for messaging, they may make so much noise that we don't need to delay for messaging. 😂 I believe major miners have known of this since quite some time now. Results of miners/vals on testnets might not be indicative of actual miner knowledge fyi condor is just trying to influence the decision to make money on polymarket "I believe major minors" nearly burned us with the Muir Glacier fork. We did that with basically no service provider input and the feedback was the timing was problematic. If we have actual service provider and miner feedback that an earlier release is preferred then that's great. But too often we make these calls just on client team input without sufficient "downstream" considerations. For the major clients (Geth, Besu, etc.) when will the releases be ready for download? It would be good to have a chance to test the new releases on testnet for at least a week before mainnet lands. I would be okay with pushing for this reason if we had an actual plan for doing this communication that required an extra week. I'm not a fan of adding a week of continued non-communication in hopes that the extra week will result in mining pools intuiting that we need them to do something. And if we had an actual communication plan, it feels unlikely that executing on it would require 4 weeks instead of 3. FYI: June 26 issue of Week in Ethereum News we had August 4 as tentative upgrade date based on last Core Devs call. So that date was out there publicly, if that helps.
